subject: BrightLayer demo — recommended model shortlist & next steps
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-01-15T12:03:00-08:00
Subject: BrightLayer demo — recommended model shortlist & next steps

Thanks again for your time today — quick recap and a recommended path to a tight POC. Appreciate the focus on latency for in-product suggestions and the high bar on hallucination for regulatory copy.

TL;DR recommendation (shortlist):
- Option A: RL-Redwood-13B-8q (recommended starter) — best balance for your 95th-pct latency target (~120ms/token on our Dedicated pool) and cost at expected volume. Strong on factuality with evals on your prompt set.
- Option B: RL-Redwood-70B-INT8 (higher quality) — noticeably better on complex multi-step reasoning, ~2x cost, 20–30% higher latency. Good if accuracy trumps cost.
- Option C: Open-Compact-13B-q4 (cost-optimized) — lowest cost, lowest latency; acceptable on short answers but higher risk for hallucination on long-form outputs.

Why these three: we prioritized (1) 95th-pct latency under 300ms for interactive suggestions, (2) cost per 1k tokens at your forecasted QPS, and (3) factuality on the clinical/medical terminology you demoed. Benchmarks attached (latency CSV) and prompt set v1 attached for reproducibility.

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) Please confirm which Option to pilot (A / B / C).
2) Confirm target 95th-pct latency and sample traffic profile (tokens per request, % long-form) so we can size Dedicated pool and caching.
3) Security: Alyssa — we flagged data retention & audit-log requirements. We can provide SOC2 artifacts and discuss a Private deployment for audit workloads.
4) Ops: we propose a 3-week POC: week 1 — focused benchmarks and regression checks using your prompt set; week 2 — integrate inference route + canary; week 3 — production-readiness checklist + mutual action plan (attached).

Attachments: brightlayer_prompt_set_v1.json; latency-benchmarks-2028-01-15.csv; mutual_action_plan_BrightLayer.pdf

If it helps, I can book a 30 min technical deep-dive with Monica and our runtime lead Tuesday or Wednesday.

Thanks — looking forward to next steps.

— Priyom

Priyom — thanks for the clear recap. Helpful. A couple quick clarifications before we lock a pilot model: 

- For Option A you called out ~120ms/token (95th pct) on Dedicated. Can you confirm what sequence length distribution that assumes? Our median request today is ~400 tokens but top-10% approaches 2,000 tokens during report generation.
- Cost: can you provide an estimated cost range for Option A vs C at ~1.2M tokens/month? Ballpark is fine; we need to show this to finance.
- Quality/regression: we liked the hallucination mitigation you demoed. How do you propose we guard against regressions when you iterate models or we move from 13B->70B? Concrete checkpointing + eval thresholds?

Also, Alyssa flagged that we need an initial answer on retention: how long do request logs stay in Hosted by default and what are the options for Private retention windows?

If we can get those answers by EOD Monday our PM will approve the MOP and sign the mutual action plan.

— Samir

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>

Subject: Fwd: BrightLayer demo — recommended model shortlist & next steps (internal ops notes)

Internal ops note — copying key bits for the pilot plan: 

- Sequence assumptions: the 120ms/token number for Option A above assumes 512-token sequences and a Dedicated worker with NVLink-d GPU pool and continuous batching. For longer sequences (~2k) expect per-token latency to increase ~1.6x; the 95th-pct will likely be ~190–200ms/token. We can mitigate by enabling prefix/KV caching for repeated context and by setting a max_allowed_context for suggestion endpoints.
- Cost estimate (rough): Option A ~ $1,200–1,700 per 1M tokens (includes Dedicated amortized infra); Option C ~ $420–700 per 1M tokens. Option B ~ $2,500–3,500 per 1M tokens. These are estimates; I'll produce a short cost sensitivity sheet once Samir confirms monthly volume.
- Regression guardrails: propose the following minimal set for the POC:
  * Baseline evals with BrightLayer prompt set (attached) + 100 held-out safety/regression prompts.
  * Automated nightly regression job: generate on stable seed, compare factuality F1 + hallucination rate. Fail the rollout if hallucination increases >5% or factuality drops >3 points.
  * Canary rollout: 5% traffic for 48 hours, rollback on metric degradation.
- Security/retention: Hosted default retention is 30 days for request logs; Private deployment can be configured to 0–90 days per contract. For regulated outputs we recommend Private with customer-managed KMS.

Action items I can take this week: produce cost sensitivity CSV and a canary config template; set up a sandbox Dedicated pool for initial benchmarks.

— Monica
